author: Priyanka Patel
title: AI TikTok Racism: Viral Videos & Concerns
text:
AI-Generated Racist Videos Flood Social Media, Sparking Concerns About Google’s Veo 3 Millions of users have viewed racist videos appearing on platforms like TikTok, YouTube, and Instagram, with evidence suggesting they were created using Google’s AI video generation tool , Veo 3. The videos, flagged by the nonprofit media watchdog Media Matters , are filled with harmful racist tropes , particularly targeting Black individuals, alongside antisemitic content and depictions of immigrants and Asian people.
A recent report from Media Matters details the proliferation of these videos, with one clip alone garnering 14.2 million views. The organization identified the videos as being generated by Veo 3 due to the presence of a distinctive “Veo” watermark in the corner of the clips. Further confirmation came from users including relevant hashtags , captions, or usernames referencing Veo 3 or artificial intelligence in their posts.
Veo 3 and the Rise of AI-Generated Harmful Content Launched in May, Veo 3 allows users to create short-form AI video and audio content simply by inputting a text prompt. Google states on its website that the tool is designed to “block harmful requests and results.” However, the emergence of these videos raises serious questions about the effectiveness of those safeguards. The identified clips were consistently short, lasting only eight seconds, or comprised of multiple segments each no longer than eight seconds – a limitation inherent in Veo 3’s current capabilities.
Platform Responses and Ongoing Concerns TikTok has taken action, stating it “proactively enforce[s] robust rules against hateful speech and behavior” and has removed the accounts identified in the Media Matters report. According to a statement from TikTok spokesperson Ariane de Selliers, provided on July 2nd, many of these accounts were already banned prior to the report’s publication.
However, the problem extends beyond TikTok. The Verge discovered some of the same videos on YouTube , albeit with fewer views, while Wired identified similar content on Instagram . This suggests a broader issue with the spread of AI-generated hate speech across multiple social media platforms.
Google Remains Silent Despite repeated requests, Google has not yet issued a public comment regarding the situation. This silence has fueled criticism and concerns about the company’s responsibility in addressing the misuse of its technology.
The rapid spread of these videos underscores the challenges of moderating AI-generated content and the potential for malicious actors to exploit powerful tools like Veo 3 to disseminate harmful ideologies. The incident serves as a stark reminder of the need for ongoing vigilance and proactive measures to mitigate the risks associated with the evolving landscape of artificial intelligence.
